mainTopic: The shape of the world and the winds, facing south or north, and then neighbor damages: mustard and bees, a tree near a בור, and רבי יוסי's 'arrows' exception.
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא about the shape of the world. רבי אליעזר says it is like an אכסדרה open on the north, so at night the sun rises above the sky. רבי יהושע says it is a closed dome, so at night the sun goes behind it. Each view gets support from פסוקים, and the גמרא explains that the south wind brings both gentle rain and harmful downpours. Then come teachings about the winds and rain: the north wind makes gold cheap, and since the חורבן the south wind brings no rain and rain no longer comes from the 'good storehouse.' רבי יצחק and רבי יהושע בן לוי discuss facing south for wisdom and north for wealth. The גמרא settles this with the שכינה being in the west and explains which way people in בבל should face. The גמרא then returns to the משנה: רבי יוסי says mustard need not be moved away from bees, because the bees damage the mustard too. A new משנה sets how far a tree must be from a neighbor's בור, depending on who came first. The הלכה follows רבי יוסי that each person may use his own land. But רבי יוסי agrees about 'his own arrows,' meaning direct damage, as in the case of the sesame pressers who shook פאפי יונאה's mansion. The amud ends by asking how much shaking counts, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: The world is like a porch open on the north
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the world is like an אכסדרה, closed on three sides and open on the north. When the sun reaches the northwest corner, it turns and rises above the sky.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The world] is like a porch. The north side is not closed off. When the sun reaches the northwest corner, it bends and goes up above the sky.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא, continuing רבי אליעזר's description of the shape of the world. He explains where the sun goes at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אכסדרה has walls on three sides and is open on the fourth. For רבי אליעזר the open side is the north. So the sun never passes along the north. Once it reaches the northwest corner, it climbs above the sky and travels back to the east during the night.

keyTerms.meaning: A porch or veranda, closed on three sides and open on one
Closed in, surrounded by a wall
The sky, the dome of heaven

phrases.english: is similar to a porch,
phrases.notes: Right before this, רבי אליעזר began: 'the world...'. So read it as 'the world is like a porch'.

phrases.english: and the northern side is not enclosed,
and once the sun reaches
the northwestern corner –
it bends and rises
above the sky.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַכְסַדְרָה הוּא דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from before this section, where רבי אליעזר began describing the world.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world is open on the north. At night the sun rises above the sky instead of passing along the north.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: The world is like a closed dome
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע disagrees. He says the world is like a קובה, closed on all four sides. At night the sun goes around outside, behind the northern wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: The world is like a small tent, and the north side is closed too. When the sun reaches the northwest corner, it circles around and goes behind the dome.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the opposing view of רבי יהושע about the shape of the world and the sun's path at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the north side is also closed. So the sun does not go up above the sky. Instead it goes out and travels around the back of the dome, outside the northern wall, until it reaches the east again.

keyTerms.meaning: A small tent or dome, closed on all sides

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two views. רבי אליעזר: the north is open, and the sun goes up OVER the sky at night. רבי יהושע: the north is closed, and the sun goes AROUND behind the dome at night.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua says:
the world is similar to a small tent,
and the northern side is enclosed,
and once the sun reaches
the northwestern corner –
it circles around and goes back behind the dome;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבי אליעזר in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world is closed on all sides. At night the sun circles behind the dome, outside the north wall.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's proof from the verse in קהלת
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in קהלת says the sun goes south and then turns north. רבי יהושע reads this as the sun going south by day and north by night, behind the dome. He reads the 'circuits' as the east and west sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'It goes toward the south and turns to the north.' 'It goes toward the south' is during the day. 'And turns to the north' is at night. 'Round and round goes the wind, and on its circuits the wind returns.' These are the east side and the west side. Sometimes the sun goes around them, and sometimes it travels across them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק as support for רבי יהושע. The פסוק says the sun goes to the north, which fits his idea that it passes behind the northern wall at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sun 'turns to the north', it must actually travel along the north. That matches רבי יהושע, who says the sun goes around the back of the dome on the north. The word רוח is read here as 'side' (direction), not 'wind'. The sun sometimes circles the east and west sides out of sight, and sometimes travels across them where we can see it.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
Here: side or direction (it can also mean wind)

phrases.english: as it is stated: "It goes toward the south,
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:6

phrases.english: and turns about to the north, etc.";
"It goes toward the south" – during the day.
"And turns about to the north" – at night.
"Round and round goes the wind,
and on its circuits the wind returns" –
these are the face of the east and the face of the west,
that sometimes it circles around them
and sometimes it travels across them.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the sun.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: הוֹלֵךְ אֶל דָּרוֹם, וְסוֹבֵב אֶל צָפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for רבי יהושע's view.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע's claim that the sun travels along the north at night, behind the dome.
steps.raayaSupportSource: קהלת 1:6: 'It goes toward the south and turns about to the north.'

steps.title: Proof for רבי אליעזר from verses in איוב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with 'He used to say.' The גמרא notes that this part follows רבי אליעזר. פסוקים from איוב are matched to the four directions, showing that the north is an open side.
steps.simpleTranslation: He used to say (this follows רבי אליעזר): 'Out of the chamber comes the storm' is the southern side. 'And cold out of the scattered places' is the northern side. 'By the breath of God ice is given' is the western side. 'And the breadth of the waters is straitened' is the eastern side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא briefly breaks in to tell us that the next statement matches רבי אליעזר. Then the ברייתא matches four phrases from איוב to the four directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The south is called a 'chamber' (חדר), a closed room, because it is enclosed together with the other walls. The north is called מזרים, 'scattered' or open places, from which the cold comes. This fits רבי אליעזר's view that the north is open, like an אכסדרה.

keyTerms.meaning: We have come to (this matches the view of)
Scattered or open places (here, the north)

phrases.english: He would say –
we have arrived at Rabbi Eliezer:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is saying this next part fits רבי אליעזר's view that the north side is open.

phrases.english: "Out of the chamber comes the storm" –
phrases.notes: איוב 37:9

phrases.english: this is the southern side.
"And cold out of the scattered places" –
this is the northern side.
"By the breath of God ice is given" –
phrases.notes: איוב 37:10

phrases.english: this is the western side.
"And the breadth of the waters is straitened" –
this is the eastern side.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר – אֲתָאן לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves back from רבי יהושע's proof to a teaching that fits רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view that the north side of the world is open.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 37:9-10, which calls the south a 'chamber' and the north 'scattered places'.

steps.title: Challenge: Doesn't the southern wind bring the rain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading that water comes from the east. A known teaching says the southern wind brings the rain and makes plants grow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say: The southern wind brings up showers and makes grass grow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. רבי אליעזר just linked water to the eastern wind, yet another teaching says the rain comes from the southern wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As Rashi explains, the clash is about rain. רבי אליעזר read 'ורחב מים במוצק' as the eastern wind, the one that brings water. But a teaching from 'the Master' says the southern wind brings רביבים, the showers that help plants grow. So which wind brings the rain?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the Master say (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
the southern wind brings up showers
and makes grass grow!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 4 that links water to the eastern wind.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'from the chamber comes the storm' refers to the southern wind.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known teaching says the south wind is helpful, bringing gentle rain and growth. That seems to contradict calling it a harmful storm.

steps.title: Answer: Gentle rain versus a downpour
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. Gentle rain comes from the south, and pouring rain comes from the east.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is when the rain comes gently. That one is when it pours down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each source describes a different kind of rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As Rashi explains, gentle rain (ניחותא) comes from the south, and that is the rain that makes plants grow. A heavy downpour (שפיכותא) comes from the east, as the פסוק says 'מים במוצק', water poured out. So both sources are true.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (there is no contradiction)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: the world is like a porch open on the north, and at night the sun goes above the sky. רבי יהושע: the world is a closed dome, and at night the sun goes behind it. Gentle rain comes from the south; pouring rain comes from the east.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this is when the rain comes gently,
that is when it comes pouring down.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source describes a different kind of rain.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rain seemed to be credited to two different winds, the east and the south.
steps.terutzMaskana: Gentle rain comes with the southern wind and downpours come with the eastern wind, so both sources are correct.

steps.title: The north wind makes gold cheap
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains the פסוק 'Out of the north comes gold' as the north wind making gold lose its value, and supports the meaning with a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What does the פסוק 'Out of the north comes gold' mean? It is the north wind, which makes gold cheap. A similar word appears in the פסוק 'Those who pour out gold from the bag.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues talking about the winds. רב חסדא gives a new reading of a פסוק in איוב about the north.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'from the north comes gold' sounds like the north brings riches. רב חסדא reads it the other way: the north wind makes gold מַזֶּלֶת, cheap, so it buys less. The פסוק in ישעיהו uses the same root זל for gold being poured out freely, which backs up his reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who pour out or spend freely
What is the meaning of what is written?

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
What is the meaning of what is written: "Out of the north comes gold"?
phrases.notes: איוב 37:22

phrases.english: This is the northern wind
which makes gold cheap.
And so it says:
"Those who pour out gold from the bag."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 46:6. The same word זל shows up here, so it backs up רב חסדא's reading.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the directions and their winds, which was opened by the פסוקים from איוב matched to the four directions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The north wind lowers the value of gold.

steps.title: Since the חורבן the south wind brings no rain
steps.stepSummary: רפרם בר פפא quotes רב חסדא: from the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, the south wind has not brought rain. He proves it from פסוקים showing that 'right' means south.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, the south wind has not brought rain. The פסוק says 'He cut on the right and there was hunger,' and another פסוק says 'North and right, You created them,' which shows that 'right' means south.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching about the south wind. Since the חורבן, the south wind no longer brings rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא said the south wind brings rain. Here we learn that this blessing stopped with the חורבן. The proof has two parts: one פסוק says hunger was decreed on the 'right,' and a second פסוק pairs 'right' with north, so 'right' must mean south.

keyTerms.meaning: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed

steps.confusionAlert: 'Right' here is not your right hand. When you face east, your right side is south. That is why the second פסוק is needed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa said that Rav Chisda said:
From the day the Temple was destroyed
the southern wind has not brought rain,
as it says: "He decreed on the right, and there was hunger,
and he ate on the left and they were not satisfied,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 9:19

phrases.english: and it is written: "North and right, You created them."
phrases.notes: תהלים 89:13. 'Right' is paired with north, so it must mean south.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the earlier point that the south wind brings rain, and adds that this stopped after the חורבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the חורבן, the south wind does not bring rain.

steps.title: Rain no longer comes from the good storehouse
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching from the same chain: since the חורבן, rain no longer comes from the 'good storehouse.' That only happens when Israel does ה׳'s will and lives on its land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא also said in the name of רב חסדא: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, rain does not come from the good storehouse. The פסוק says 'ה׳ will open for you His good storehouse.' When Israel does ה׳'s will and lives on its land, rain comes from the good storehouse. When Israel is not living on its land, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching from the same chain of rabbis. It is again about rain after the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק promises a 'good storehouse' of rain. It is a blessing that depends on Israel's situation. The גמרא sets the conditions: doing ה׳'s will and living on the land. Since the חורבן, Israel is not settled on its land, so the good storehouse is closed.
steps.whatToRemember: Both teachings of רפרם בר פפא connect the loss of good rain to the חורבן.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: And Rafram bar Pappa said that Rav Chisda said:
From the day the Temple was destroyed
the rains do not come down from the good storehouse,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״יִפְתַּח ה׳ לְךָ אֶת אוֹצָרוֹ הַטּוֹב״ –
phrases.english: as it says: "ה׳ will open for you His good storehouse" —
phrases.notes: דברים 28:12

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: at a time when Israel does the will of ה׳,
and Israel is settled on its land —
rain comes down from the good storehouse;

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁרוּיִין עַל אַדְמָתָם –
phrases.english: at a time when Israel is not settled on its land —
rain does not come down from the good storehouse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching by the same speakers on the same theme of rain after the חורבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain comes from the good storehouse only when Israel does ה׳'s will and lives on its land. Since the חורבן, it does not.

steps.title: Face south for wisdom, north for wealth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that someone who wants wisdom should face south, and someone who wants wealth should face north. The memory aid is the שלחן in the north and the מנורה in the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Someone who wants to become wise should face south, and someone who wants to become rich should face north. Your memory aid is that the שלחן was in the north and the מנורה was in the south.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching that links the directions to blessings. South brings wisdom, and north brings wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק ties each direction to a blessing. The memory aid comes from the בית המקדש. The שלחן with the bread stood in the north and stands for wealth. The מנורה with its light stood in the south and stands for wisdom.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
One who wants to become wise should face south,
and one who wants to become rich should face north,
and your memory aid is:
the Table in the north and the Menorah in the south.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיַּחְכִּים יַדְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from winds and rain to the blessings linked with facing each direction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Facing south brings wisdom, and facing north brings wealth.

steps.title: Always face south, since wisdom brings wealth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says a person should always face south, because becoming wise also leads to becoming rich. He proves this from a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A person should always face south. Once he becomes wise, he will also become rich. The פסוק says about the תורה: 'Long life is in her right hand, and in her left hand are wealth and honor.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי offers a different approach from רבי יצחק. He says you do not need to choose, so always face south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק made it sound like a choice between wisdom and wealth. רבי יהושע בן לוי says wisdom brings wealth along with it, so south is always the better direction. The פסוק shows that the תורה holds riches and honor too, in her left hand.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק: south for wisdom, north for wealth. רבי יהושע בן לוי: always south, because wisdom brings wealth with it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One should always face south,
because once he becomes wise, he becomes rich —
as it says: "Length of days is in her right hand,
phrases.notes: משלי 3:16. The 'her' in the פסוק is the תורה, or wisdom.

phrases.english: in her left hand are wealth and honor."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם יַדְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יצחק's division. He says south covers both blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Always face south, because wisdom brings wealth with it.

steps.title: But the Divine Presence is in the west
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the advice to face south, because רבי יהושע בן לוי himself said the שכינה is in the west.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The שכינה is in the west!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. How can רבי יהושע בן לוי tell us to always face south when he also said the שכינה rests in the west?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11, רבי יהושע בן לוי said a person should always face south. But he also taught that the שכינה is in the west, which suggests we should face west. The same Sage seems to be saying two opposite things.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The Divine Presence is in the west!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 11 with another teaching from the same Sage
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's advice to always face south
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the שכינה is in the west, one should face west, not south

steps.title: Turn slightly to the side
steps.stepSummary: The answer: face south but tilt slightly toward the west.
steps.simpleTranslation: He means that one turns slightly to the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction: you face south, but tilt a little toward the west.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both teachings are kept. Facing south-west lets a person face toward wisdom (south) and still show respect for the שכינה in the west.

phrases.english: That he turns slightly to the side.
phrases.notes: He faces south but tilts a bit toward the west.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמַצְדֵּד אַצְדּוֹדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: both directions are partly kept
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Facing south means ignoring the שכינה in the west
steps.terutzMaskana: Face south while tilting slightly west

steps.title: People living north of ארץ ישראל should face south
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא tells רב אשי that since he lives north of ארץ ישראל, he should face south.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said to רב אשי: People like you, who live north of ארץ ישראל, should face south.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives practical direction advice to רב אשי, who lives in בבל: face south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For people in בבל, facing south means facing toward ארץ ישראל. This is a direction rule based on where you live, not just on the idea of wisdom from the south.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said to Rav Ashi:
People such as you,
who live to the north of Eretz Yisrael –
should face south.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical direction rule for people in בבל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those living north of ארץ ישראל should face south

steps.title: How do we know בבל is north of ארץ ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that בבל lies north of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that בבל is located north of ארץ ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know רבי חנינא's geography is right. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא's advice depends on בבל being north of ארץ ישראל. The גמרא wants a source for that fact.

phrases.english: And from where do we know
that Babylonia is located to the north of Eretz Yisrael?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא לַן דְּבָבֶל לִצְפוֹנָהּ דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָיְימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind Step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing בבל is north of ארץ ישראל

steps.title: Proof from ירמיהו: evil comes from the north
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in ירמיהו says evil will come from the north, referring to בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: Out of the north evil shall break forth upon all the inhabitants of the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק: the disaster that came from בבל is described as coming from the north.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prophecy is about בבל destroying ירושלים. Since the פסוק calls it 'from the north,' בבל must be north of ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: Face south, tilting slightly west; for people in בבל, south is toward ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"Out of the north evil shall break forth
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 1:14

phrases.english: upon all the inhabitants of the land."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב מִצָּפוֹן תִּפָּתַח הָרָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in ירמיהו describes the attack from בבל as coming from the north

steps.title: ר׳ יוסי: the mustard grower can blame the bees
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה, a ברייתא says ר׳ יוסי does not require moving mustard away from bees, since the bees damage the mustard too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One must keep flax-soaking water away from vegetables, etc. A ברייתא taught: ר׳ יוסי permits keeping mustard near bees, because the owner can say: Before you tell me to move my mustard away from your bees, move your bees away from my mustard, since they come and eat my mustard plants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about distancing damaging things and brings a ברייתא with ר׳ יוסי's view on mustard and bees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה required moving mustard away from bees, because mustard ruins the honey. ר׳ יוסי argues that the bees also damage the mustard by eating it. Since each side harms the other, neither can force the other to move.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a principle: when two neighbors damage each other, one cannot simply demand that the other move.

phrases.aramaic: מַרְחִיקִין אֶת הַמִּשְׁרָה מִן הַיָּרָק וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: One must distance the flax-soaking water from vegetables, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה, which also says to keep mustard away from bees.

phrases.english: It was taught:
Rabbi Yosei permits in the case of mustard,
because he can say to him:
Before you tell me:
Distance your mustard from my bees;
distance your bees from my mustard,
for they come and eat the tender shoots of my mustard.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְחִיקִין אֶת הַמִּשְׁרָה מִן הַיָּרָק וְכוּ׳ תָּנָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר בַּחַרְדָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about directions and returns to the earlier משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ר׳ יוסי: mustard need not be moved away from bees, since the bees damage the mustard too

steps.title: New משנה: how far a tree must be from a cistern
steps.stepSummary: A tree must be 25 אמות from a בור; a carob or sycamore must be 50 אמות, whether above or to the side.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One must keep a tree 25 אמות away from a בור, and a carob or sycamore 50 אמות, whether it is above or to the side.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the distance a tree must be kept from a neighbor's cistern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tree roots spread and can break into a cistern. Carob and sycamore trees have wider roots, so they need double the distance. The rule applies whether the tree is above the cistern or level with it on the side.

keyTerms.meaning: Cistern, a pit for storing water

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מַרְחִיקִין אֶת הָאִילָן מִן הַבּוֹר
phrases.english: MISHNA: One must distance a tree from a cistern
twenty-five cubits,
and for a carob or a sycamore –
fifty cubits;
whether from above or from the side.
phrases.notes: He means the tree stands higher up than the cistern, or level with it off to the side.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְחִיקִין אֶת הָאִילָן מִן הַבּוֹר עֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new case of neighbor damage
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tree must be 25 אמות from a בור; a carob or sycamore, 50 אמות

steps.title: Who came first decides whether the tree is cut
steps.stepSummary: If the בור came first, the tree is cut down and its owner is paid; if the tree came first or it is unclear, it is not cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the בור came first, the tree owner cuts it down and the בור owner pays him. If the tree came first, he does not cut it. If it is unclear which came first, he does not cut it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what happens when a tree is already too close to a cistern. It depends on which one was there first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the בור was there first, the tree must go, but the בור owner pays for it. If the tree was there first, the newcomer cannot force it to be cut. In a doubt, the tree stays, because the tree owner cannot be forced to cut it without clear proof.
steps.confusionAlert: In the case where the בור came first, the tree is cut but the בור owner pays. Do not think the tree owner loses his tree for nothing.

phrases.english: If the cistern came first –
he cuts it down and he pays money,
phrases.notes: The tree owner cuts the tree, and the cistern owner pays him for it.

phrases.english: and if the tree came first – he does not cut it down.

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק זֶה קָדַם וְסָפֵק זֶה קָדַם –
phrases.english: If it is unclear whether this came first or that came first –
he does not cut it down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הַבּוֹר קָדְמָה קוֹצֵץ וְנוֹתֵן דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with what happens when the distance was not kept
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cistern first: cut and pay. Tree first or unclear: do not cut

steps.title: ר׳ יוסי: each one works in his own property
steps.stepSummary: ר׳ יוסי says the tree is never cut, even if the בור came first, since each person is using his own land.
steps.simpleTranslation: ר׳ יוסי says: Even if the בור came first, he does not cut down the tree, because this one digs in his own property and that one plants in his own property.
steps.whatsHappening: ר׳ יוסי disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה about the case where the בור came first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says the tree must be cut if the בור was first. ר׳ יוסי says no: each owner has the right to use his own land, so the tree owner cannot be forced to cut his tree.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא: if the בור came first, cut the tree and pay. ר׳ יוסי: never cut, since each one is acting in his own land.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַבּוֹר קוֹדֶמֶת לָאִילָן –
phrases.english: Even though the cistern came before the tree –
he does not cut it down,
because this one digs in his own property
and that one plants in his own property.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַבּוֹר קוֹדֶמֶת לָאִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in Step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ר׳ יוסי: the tree is not cut even if the בור came first

steps.title: The rule applies whether the tree is above or below
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the distance applies both when the tree is above the בור and when it is below it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A ברייתא taught: This applies whether the בור is below and the tree is above, or the בור is above and the tree is below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and brings a ברייתא that widens the משנה's rule. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'whether from above.' The ברייתא makes clear that the distance is required in both directions: tree higher than the בור, and tree lower than the בור.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
whether the cistern is below and the tree is above,
or whether the cistern is above and the tree is below.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא בֵּין שֶׁהַבּוֹר לְמַטָּה וְאִילָן לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה's phrase 'from above'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The distance applies whether the tree is above or below the בור

steps.title: Why does a lower tree harm a higher cistern?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why a higher tree harms a lower בור, but asks why a lower tree should harm a higher בור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense when the בור is below and the tree above: the roots spread and damage the בור. But when the בור is above and the tree below, why?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the second half of the ברייתא. A tree below the cistern seems unable to hurt it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the tree is higher, its roots grow down into the cistern and damage it. But when the tree is lower, the roots grow down and away from the cistern, so it seems there should be no damage and no need to keep a distance.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (in the first case)

phrases.english: It makes sense when the cistern is below and the tree is above –
the roots extend
and damage the cistern.
But when the cistern is above and the tree is below,
why?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בּוֹר לְמַטָּה וְאִילָן לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second case of the ברייתא in Step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a tree below the בור must also be distanced
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Roots grow downward, so a lower tree should not reach a higher cistern

steps.title: The roots loosen the soil and ruin the cistern floor
steps.stepSummary: רבי חגא in the name of רבי יוסי explains that the roots hollow out the ground and damage the cistern's floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חגא said in the name of רבי יוסי: Because the roots make holes in the ground and ruin the floor of the בור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: even a lower tree causes damage, because its roots weaken the ground under the cistern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The damage is not from roots breaking through the cistern's walls. The roots dig through and loosen the soil, so the ground under the cistern's floor gets weak and the floor is damaged.
steps.whatToRemember: A tree must be kept away from a בור whether it is higher or lower, because lower roots weaken the ground beneath the בור.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חַגָּא בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chagga said in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
Because they make holes in the ground
and ruin the floor of the cistern.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חַגָּא בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּחְלִידִין אֶת הַקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different kind of damage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A lower tree cannot damage a higher cistern
steps.terutzMaskana: The roots loosen the soil and damage the cistern's floor from below

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's view again, and רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that the הלכה follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: even if the pit was there before the tree, the tree owner does not have to cut it down, because one dug in his own land and the other planted in his own land. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי יוסי's words from the משנה so it can give the final ruling on them. שמואל says we follow רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeat is not an accident: the גמרא brings the line back in order to rule on it. With the ruling set, the tree stays, even if the בור came first. This prepares the next step, where רב אשי will limit how far this ruling goes.

keyTerms.meaning: he need not cut down (the tree)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law: who came first does not decide the matter, because each person may use his own land.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
phrases.notes: This is the line from the משנה in Step 20, brought back so the גמרא can rule on it.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַבּוֹר קוֹדֶמֶת לְאִילָן –
phrases.english: Even though the pit came before the tree,
he need not cut it down,
for this one digs within his own,
and that one plants within his own.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל הלכה כרבי יוסי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about a tree below the בור and returns to רבי יוסי's opinion in order to rule on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: the tree is not cut down even if the בור came first, since each one is using his own land.

steps.title: רבי יוסי agrees when the damage comes straight from your own action
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that in רב כהנא's study hall they taught that רבי יוסי agrees a person is responsible for 'his arrows', meaning damage that comes directly from his own act.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When we were in רב כהנא's study hall, we used to say that רבי יוסי agrees when it comes to a person's own arrows.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי puts a limit on רבי יוסי's rule. 'Each one in his own land' does not cover a case where your action shoots damage straight into your neighbor's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a tree, the roots slowly spread on their own, so the tree owner is not seen as directly causing the damage. But when a person's own act sends force into the neighbor's land, like an arrow he shot, even רבי יוסי says he must stop or move away. So רבי יוסי's view is not a blanket permission to do anything in your own land.

keyTerms.meaning: 'his own arrows', meaning damage that comes directly from a person's own action
the study hall of a teacher

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב אשי is arguing with רבי יוסי or with the ruling. He is explaining how far רבי יוסי's own view goes: it covers slow, indirect harm like roots, but not harm you send out yourself.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When we were in the study hall of Rav Kahana,
we would say:
Rabbi Yosei concedes regarding his own arrows.
phrases.notes: 'Arrows' is a picture: harm a person sends straight from himself into his neighbor's property, like shooting an arrow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מודי רבי יוסי בגירי דידיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling just given in favor of רבי יוסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even רבי יוסי holds a person liable to stop or move away when his own action directly sends damage into his neighbor's property.

steps.title: Sesame pressers shaking a neighbor's mansion
steps.stepSummary: פאפי יונאה built a mansion, and nearby sesame pressers' pounding made it shake. רב אשי applied the 'arrows' rule to his case.
steps.simpleTranslation: פאפי יונאה had been poor and became rich, and he built a mansion. There were sesame pressers in his neighborhood, and when they pounded sesame, his mansion shook. He came before רב אשי, who told him: When we were in רב כהנא's study hall, we used to say that רבי יוסי agrees when it comes to a person's own arrows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case that shows the 'arrows' rule in action. רב אשי rules that the pressers must stop, because their pounding directly shakes the neighbor's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pressers are working in their own space, so you might think רבי יוסי's rule protects them. But the force of their pounding goes straight into the mansion, just like an arrow, so they are responsible. The story shows that the 'arrows' rule is used in practice.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule follows רבי יוסי, so each person may use his own land. But if your action directly sends harm into your neighbor's property (גירי דיליה), you must stop, as with the sesame pressers whose pounding shook the mansion.

phrases.english: Pappei Yona'a
was poor and became rich.
He built a mansion.
There were these pressers in his neighborhood,
so that when they would pound sesame,
his mansion would shake.
He came before Rav Ashi.
He said to him:
phrases.notes: Here it is רב אשי answering פאפי יונאה.

phrases.english: When we were in the study hall of Rav Kahana,
we would say:
Rabbi Yosei concedes regarding his own arrows.

steps.triggerLanguage: פאפי יונאה עני והעשיר הוה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practical case where רב אשי applied the 'arrows' rule from Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sesame pressers whose pounding shakes a neighbor's house count as 'his own arrows' and must stop or move away.

steps.title: How much shaking counts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how strong the shaking must be for the house owner to be able to make the pressers move away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question: how much must the house shake for this rule to apply? It is setting up the next step, where the answer will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that shaking counts as direct damage, the גמרא wants a clear measure. Not every tiny vibration should be enough to force a neighbor to stop working, so a limit is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: and how much? (asking for a measure)

phrases.english: And how much?
phrases.notes: He means: how much must the mansion shake before the pressers have to move away?

steps.triggerLanguage: וכמה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure behind the ruling in the sesame pressers story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What amount of shaking counts as direct damage that requires the pressers to move away.
